title: Typed Residue-Interface Automata on Low-Height Asymmetric X
novelty_claim: The only live CA-adjacent claim is not that forcing is a cellular automaton, but that a frozen finite interface alphabet carrying signed residue summaries can compose exactly under one unchanged extractor and therefore act as a certificate-carrying search grammar inside low-height asymmetric X regimes.
closest_prior_art: Regional boundary-control and SAT-synthesized CA controllers
differentiation: This survives only if interface sufficiency is the explicit object under test: the same interface table must handle level-1 and level-2 without new symbols, repair passes, or hidden complexity, and it must beat matched direct no-CA search at the same description budget. Otherwise it is just H1 in narrower packaging.
easiest_falsifier: Freeze one interface alphabet and one exact extractor, enumerate the level-1 residue classes, and reject immediately if level-2 composition needs new symbols or repair, if the trace language collapses to a tiny periodic set, or if matched direct grammar search recovers the same family.
evidence_plan: Fix one low-height asymmetric X family, one exact extractor to legal (X; d_i; f_i; T; R), one symmetry quotient, and one matched baseline matrix.
Enumerate exact local residue summaries and canonical interface traces on level-1 tiles, then require the same interface table to compose level-2 instances.
Compare exact extracted score and hit rate against matched direct no-CA search with the same geometry, palette, and description budget, with hidden-complexity logging required.

budget_envelope.compute: None until the interface grammar, symmetry policy, and matched baseline matrix are frozen; after that, one narrow exact comparison only
budget_envelope.search_scope: Single interface alphabet on one low-height asymmetric corridor family
budget_envelope.web: none unless a narrow citation repair is forced

title: Affine-Core / Nonlinear-Shell Residue Automata
novelty_claim: If any CA-style mechanism survives exact extraction, the bulk should look like affine residue transport with only a tiny audited nonlinear shell at residue-isolation gates; the contribution would be to localize that shell rather than hide the real work inside unrestricted nonlinear search or solver glue.
differentiation: This is not a generic SAT wrapper and not an H2-style invariant relabeling. It survives only if the bulk remains interpretable and affine, the nonlinear shell stabilizes into a small reusable gate library on tiny exact instances, and the route still beats direct no-CA search on exact extracted score.
easiest_falsifier: Strip bulk nonlinearity and mine SAT or UNSAT motifs on tiny exact instances; kill the route if no stable gate library appears, if the shell size grows with scale, or if direct certificate search matches the same frontier under the same budget.
evidence_plan: Classify candidate local updates into affine interior pieces and nonlinear gate candidates under fixed X and one exact extractor.
Use tiny exact instances to log satisfiable motifs and UNSAT cores, keeping only motifs that stabilize into a small reusable gate set.
Require any surviving family to outperform fully affine controls, unconstrained nonlinear controls, and matched direct certificate search on exact score or hit rate per budget.

budget_envelope.compute: None until the tiny-instance audit spec is frozen; then one narrow motif audit only
budget_envelope.search_scope: Tiny exact instances on the same family IDs used by the champion route
budget_envelope.web: none unless a narrow citation repair is forced

title: Seed-Minimal Phase-Coded Defect Transport on Aperiodic Corridors
novelty_claim: Keep X fixed and try to lower seed debt through tiny aperiodic phase schedules plus typed sinks and defects, rather than by enlarging slope complexity or changing the theorem statement; the claim is purely about exact seed economics after extraction.
differentiation: This survives only if the gain remains after transposition, orientation randomization, boundary-seed thinning, and matched fixed-X baselines. Otherwise it collapses into boundary programming, local-decoder folklore, or another bounded-slope retuning story.
easiest_falsifier: Run periodic versus aperiodic phase schedules with identical X, geometry, and seed budgets, then kill the route if seed reduction disappears under transposition or orientation perturbations, or if richer interfaces or richer X are needed to keep the effect.
evidence_plan: Test height-2 and height-3 anisotropic corridors with two corner defects and one typed sink under fixed low-height asymmetric X.
Compare periodic and aperiodic phase schedules under the same extractor, geometry, and seed budget, with boundary-seed thinning and R/T perturbations.
Continue only if exact score or forced-vertex-per-seed gains survive transposed controls and matched non-CA baselines.

budget_envelope.compute: None until the fixed-X baseline matrix is frozen; then one narrow hedge pass only
budget_envelope.search_scope: Single fixed-X seed-economics hedge after the champion and backup gates
budget_envelope.web: none unless a narrow citation repair is forced
